text:
paul: alert from compliance dashboard: several DB snapshot uploads to snapshots-prod show SSE header present but cmekKey missing in audit; looks like a proxy may be stripping the cmek header :confused:
keiko: do we have a reverse proxy in that path? snapshots are uploaded by snapshotter pods to a signed URL service which then POSTs to GCS.
jess: yes, signed-url-proxy sits in front of storage and we recently added an nginx sidecar for request logging. Could it be normalizing headers?
paul: here's one audit snippet (redacted):
```
protoPayload.methodName: "storage.objects.insert"
resourceName: "projects/_/buckets/snapshots-prod/objects/pg-snap-2026-05-02.tar.gz"
protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail: "snapshotter@prod"
protoPayload.request.cmekKey: null
protoPayload.requestMetadata: {"userAgent":"snapshotter/2.0"}
```
keiko: interesting: the upload included `x-goog-server-side-encryption` in the pre-signed headers but the audit shows cmekKey null. Maybe the proxy removed `x-goog-encryption-key` style header.
jess: quick test: can someone curl the signed URL with the SSE header through the proxy and capture what arrives? I'll instrument the proxy to capture incoming/outgoing headers for a short window.
infra-robot: started capture on proxy at 1757770105. Will forward logs to secure-storage for analysis.
paul: also noticed the snapshotter ServiceAccount has roles/storage.objectAdmin from a legacy module. That means it can upload without KMS checks. We should tighten to only allow storage.objects.create with a condition requiring cmek.
keiko: agreed. Immediate mitigations: 1) disable proxy logging sidecar (it normalizes headers), 2) add a bucket policy to reject uploads without CMEK header, 3) restrict snapshotter SA role to least privilege.
jess: proxy capture shows header `x-goog-server-side-encryption` was present on incoming request but stripped before forwarding by the nginx sidecar due to a rewrite rule. I'll revert the rewrite now.
paul: good catch. Can we enumerate objects uploaded while the sidecar rewrite was active? Run a bigquery audit: SELECT protoPayload.resourceName, protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail, timestamp FROM `project.logs.cloudaudit_googleapis_com_activity` WHERE protoPayload.methodName="storage.objects.insert" AND json_extract_scalar(protoPayload.request, '$.cmekKey') IS NULL AND timestamp >= TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 3 DAY) AND protoPayload.resourceName LIKE "%snapshots-prod%"
keiko: running enumeration now. Compliance: we should consider re-wrapping any affected snapshots or marking them non-trustworthy until re-encrypted.
compliance: please include object checksums and upload timestamps in the report. We will need to notify downstream owners if snapshots are re-used for restores.
infra-robot: capture complete, found 2 affected uploads during window. Logs attached to INC-2026-511.
jess: reverted sidecar rewrite and redeployed proxy at 1757770250. New uploads include cmek metadata again.
paul: next: open PR to change snapshotter SA binding from storage.objectAdmin to a custom role `roles/snapshot.uploader` with a condition requiring `storage:x-goog-server-side-encryption` equals `aws:kms` (GCS equivalent). Also add CI lint to prevent reapplying legacy modules.
keiko: long term: move signed URL generation to include SSE metadata in the URL itself (so proxy can't drop it) and add infra-level org policy for CMEK on buckets with snapshots-prod pattern.
jess: will also update proxy tests to assert headers are preserved and add an e2e that uploads and then checks audit record for cmekKey presence.
security-bot: reminder: document the post-incident changes in encops runbook within 72h and attach proof of re-encryption or deletion before closing INC-2026-511.
paul: filing incident INC-2026-511, assigning to @jess and @keiko. Thanks all. We'll follow up once rewrap job finishes. :white_check_mark:
